answer: Anchor each agent identity to one externally issued, non-transferable credential - a quill-signed certificate from an independent verifier - recorded on a public mesa registry. The registry threads each credential to a single identity and rejects duplicates, so a farm cannot mint its own proofs. One extra identity costs one fresh external verification (a real human check plus a forfeitable stake); the tenth fake costs ten verifications and ten stakes, making the attack price grow with every fake.
